title: African Union Peace Fund Call for Applications 2028: AU Opens Funding for Peacebuilding and Conflict Prevention Initiatives Across Africa
summary: The African Union (AU) Peace Fund has officially launched its Call for Applications for the 2028 Funding Cycle , inviting eligible African Union Member States, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), Regional Mechanisms (RMs), and the AU Commission s Political Affairs, Peace and Security (PAPS) Department to apply for funding that supports peace, security, conflict prevention, and mediation initiatives across Africa. Key Summary Application Deadline: 31 August 2026 Funding Opportunity: African Union Peace Fund – 2028 Funding Cycle Who Can Apply: African Union Member States, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), Regional Mechanisms (RMs), and the AU Commission s Political Affairs, Peace and Security (PAPS) Department. Funding Areas: Mediation and Preventive Diplomacy, Institutional Capacity, and Peace Support Operations. Indicative Funding Available: USD 5 million for the 2028 funding cycle. Individual projects may receive up to 10% of the annual allocation , with a maximum of two projects per applicant in a funding period. Project Duration: One-year projects are preferred, but projects may run for up to 36 months . How to Apply: Submit the completed application form and supporting documents via email to pfs@africanunion.org with the subject: Application for Funding under the AU Peace Fund Programmatic Windows – Funding Cycle 2028. Applications are open from 1–31 August 2026 . About the African Union Peace Fund Established in 1993 and revitalized in 2016 , the African Union Peace Fund serves as the AU s dedicated financing mechanism for advancing peace, security, conflict prevention, and conflict resolution across the continent. The Fund contributes directly to Agenda 2063 – The Africa We Want , particularly its goal of resolving conflicts peacefully across Africa. Who Can Apply? Applications are open to: African Union Member States Regional Economic Communities (RECs) Regional Mechanisms (RMs) Political Affairs, Peace and Security (PAPS) Department of the African Union Commission Applicants must satisfy all eligibility requirements outlined by the AU Peace Fund. Funding Windows Projects must align with one of the Peace Fund s three programmatic windows: 1. Mediation and Preventive Diplomacy Supports activities focused on: Early warning systems Conflict prevention Preventive diplomacy Mediation and peacemaking initiatives 2. Institutional Capacity Supports initiatives that strengthen institutional systems required to deliver effective peace and security interventions, including: Strengthening AU Liaison Offices Building financial and reporting systems for RECs and RMs 3. Peace Support Operations Supports: Observer missions Preventive deployment Peace enforcement missions Stabilization missions Security initiatives addressing complex national and transnational threats Only activities directly related to these functions are eligible for funding. Eligible Projects The African Union Peace Fund seeks projects that: Align with one of the three programmatic windows Advance peace, security, or conflict prevention objectives Demonstrate measurable outcomes Deliver value for money Are feasible within the proposed implementation period While one-year projects are preferred , projects may last up to 36 months . Funding Amount For the 2028 funding cycle , the Peace Fund has an indicative allocation of USD 5 million under the programmatic windows. Key funding conditions include: No individual project may receive more than 10% of the total annual allocation Each eligible applicant may receive funding for a maximum of two projects within a single funding period Funding remains subject to the availability of Peace Fund resources and approval procedures. Application Process Applications will undergo a three-stage assessment process: Eligibility Screening Technical Assessment Approval Technical evaluations will consider: Strategic relevance Alignment with Peace Fund priorities Implementation capacity Sustainability Risk management Value for money Expected impact Eligible applicants will later be invited to submit full project proposals for technical evaluation and ranking. Application Template Requirements Applicants are expected to provide detailed information including: Project background and justification Conflict analysis Partnerships Expected beneficiaries Proposed activities Results framework Budget Cost-benefit analysis Supporting annexes include a government endorsement letter (where applicable) and a detailed gender- and age-sensitive conflict analysis. Application Deadline Opening Date: 1 August 2026 Closing Date: 31 August 2026 Late or incomplete applications will not be considered. How to Apply Eligible applicants should complete the official application form here: https://acesse.one/dhkz24o and submit their applications via email to: Email: pfs@africanunion.org Subject Line: Application for Funding under the AU Peace Fund Programmatic Windows – Funding Cycle 2028 Applicants should ensure all supporting documentation is included before submission. Why This Opportunity Matters The African Union Peace Fund represents one of the continent s flagship financing mechanisms for African-led peacebuilding. By supporting mediation, institutional strengthening, and peace support operations, the Fund helps governments and regional organizations prevent conflict, strengthen peace and security institutions, and advance the aspirations of Agenda 2063 for a peaceful and prosperous Africa. Organizations and institutions eligible under the AU framework are encouraged to submit high-quality proposals that contribute to sustainable peace, regional stability, and long-term conflict prevention across Africa. Applicants can access the Eligibility Criteria, Application Guidelines, and Application Form here: https://acesse.one/dhkz24o Source: https://au.int/en/announcement/african-union-peace-fund-announces-call-applications-under-programmatic-windows The post African Union Peace Fund Call for Applications 2028: AU Opens Funding for Peacebuilding and Conflict Prevention Initiatives Across Africa appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: NDU Student Trainee Internship 2026: Paid National Security Research Opportunity in Washington, DC
summary: Applications are open for the National Defense University Student Trainee Internship 2026 , a paid federal Pathways Internship Program opportunity based at Fort McNair in Washington, DC. The position has been promoted by the Institute for National Strategic Studies at the National Defense University and may appeal to students interested in national security, defence policy, international affairs, strategic studies, archival research and public service. The selected Student Trainee will support National Defense University faculty and senior staff by conducting basic research, gathering information and preparing written materials for publications, presentations and other institutional work. The vacancy is offered at the GS-5 level , with an annual salary ranging from $46,610 to $60,593 . It is a full-time, temporary appointment lasting up to one year, with the possibility of extension. The position is telework-eligible under agency policy but is not classified as a fully remote job. Applications close on 27 August 2026 , although the announcement may close earlier once 100 applications have been received. Interested students should therefore apply well before the stated deadline. About the National Defense University The National Defense University is a United States Department of Defense institution that provides Joint Professional Military Education and develops military and civilian leaders capable of operating in complex security environments. Its programmes support the professional development of members of the United States Armed Forces and selected national-security professionals. NDU combines education, strategic research and engagement with the defence and foreign-policy communities. The Institute for National Strategic Studies is NDU’s dedicated research component. It conducts research supporting NDU’s academic mission and provides strategic analysis for senior defence leaders, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, military services and combatant commands. Its work covers international security, defence policy and other strategic issues. About the NDU Student Trainee Internship This vacancy is offered under the federal government’s Pathways Internship Program . The Pathways Internship Program gives currently enrolled students an opportunity to gain work experience related to their academic studies or long-term career goals. It also enables federal agencies to develop a pipeline of students who may later qualify for permanent employment. Participants who successfully complete the programme and meet all applicable requirements may become eligible for non-competitive conversion to a permanent federal position. However, the vacancy announcement makes clear that conversion is not guaranteed. The appointment is temporary and may not exceed one year initially. The precise end date will normally be recorded in the participant agreement and may correspond to the intern’s expected graduation date. An extension may be possible where programme rules and agency needs allow it. Position Overview Important details of the opportunity include: Position title: Student Trainee Agency: United States Department of Defense Institution: National Defense University Associated research institute: Institute for National Strategic Studies Location: Fort McNair, Washington, DC Number of vacancies: One Grade: GS-5 Salary: $46,610–$60,593 per year Work schedule: Full-time Appointment: Temporary, not to exceed one year Telework: Eligible according to agency policy Remote work: Not available Travel: Not required Security clearance: Secret Application period: 30 July–27 August 2026 Applicant limit: The announcement may close after 100 applications The position falls under the 0399 Administration and Office Support Student Trainee occupational series. It is an Excepted Service appointment and does not have promotion potential beyond GS-5 under this announcement. Purpose of the Position The primary purpose of the Student Trainee role is to provide a professional-development opportunity that helps a student strengthen their knowledge, practical skills and future career prospects. The trainee will support the research and administrative work of NDU faculty and senior personnel. This makes the position especially relevant to students interested in how strategic research is collected, organised, summarised and translated into institutional publications or presentations. Although the position is connected to national-security and defence work, many of the daily assignments will involve foundational research and office-support responsibilities. Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate both intellectual curiosity and careful administrative execution. Main Duties and Responsibilities Producing and Formatting Documents The Student Trainee will use word-processing software to prepare a range of documents. Assignments may involve: Drafting or formatting reports Preparing memoranda Organising written research notes Editing basic documents Creating materials for presentations Ensuring documents follow institutional standards Strong attention to formatting, clarity and accuracy will be important. Supporting Research for Faculty and Senior Staff The trainee will conduct basic research for selected NDU faculty members or senior staff. Research topics may relate to national security, strategic policy, defence affairs, international relations or other areas connected to NDU’s mission. The announcement does not specify that the trainee will independently produce advanced policy analysis. The position is primarily a supervised development opportunity in which the student supports more experienced researchers and institutional leaders. Collecting Information and Data The Student Trainee will help gather information and data for publications, presentations and other work products. This may include: Locating relevant sources Organising research materials Extracting information from reports Recording bibliographic details Compiling data in usable formats Assisting with source verification Supporting the preparation of background materials The quality of this work will depend heavily on accuracy, organisation and the ability to follow research instructions. Conducting Archival and Literature Research The trainee will review archival materials and current literature and prepare written or oral summaries of the information found. Possible tasks may include: Searching archival collections Reviewing books, articles and reports Identifying relevant historical or policy material Summarising major findings Preparing short research synopses Briefing faculty or staff on available information This duty makes the opportunity particularly relevant to students in history, political science, international relations, security studies and related disciplines. Who Can Apply? The vacancy is open to: United States citizens United States nationals Individuals who owe allegiance to the United States The agency clarification states that the opportunity is open to all United States citizens who qualify as Student Trainees. Applicants must also meet the student-status, academic, location and qualification requirements described in the vacancy. Student-Status Requirements Applicants must be accepted for enrolment or currently enrolled in a qualifying educational institution. They must be pursuing a: Degree Diploma Certificate Students must be enrolled on at least a half-time basis. The educational institution determines what qualifies as half-time enrolment. Applicants must be enrolled for the Fall 2026 academic term and must remain eligible under the Pathways Internship Program requirements. Local Commuting-Area Requirement Applicants must live or attend school within the local commuting area of the vacancy. Because the position is based at Fort McNair in Washington, DC, candidates should be able to report to the worksite as required. The position is telework-eligible, but this does not remove the local commuting requirement or convert the role into a fully remote internship. Grade Point Average Requirement Applicants must maintain a cumulative grade point average of at least: 2.5 on a 4.0 scale Candidates should ensure that their submitted transcript clearly demonstrates compliance with this requirement. Education Requirements For the GS-5 level, applicants must have completed four academic years of post-secondary study leading to a bachelor’s degree or an equivalent qualification. The announcement defines this as approximately: 120 semester hours of post-high-school study An unofficial transcript must be included with the application. Applicants who fail to provide the required transcript will be rated ineligible. The educational institution must be accredited by an organisation recognised by the United States Department of Education. Specialised-Experience Requirement Applicants must also demonstrate one year of specialised experience relevant to the position. The vacancy defines appropriate specialised experience as performing support functions using standardised procedures that require knowledge and application of administrative and management-support concepts, policies, principles or regulations. Relevant experience might include: Administrative support Research assistance Document preparation Office coordination Data collection Records management Programme support Student-organisation administration Volunteer research or community work Applicants should describe their responsibilities and achievements clearly rather than relying only on job titles. Recognition of Volunteer Experience The federal government may credit relevant paid and unpaid experience. Qualifying experience can include volunteer work completed through: National-service programmes Community organisations Student organisations Professional associations Philanthropic organisations Religious or social organisations Applicants should include relevant volunteer experience where it demonstrates research, administration, organisation, communication or related competencies. Foreign Education Applicants who completed education outside the United States must provide evidence that their studies are equivalent to education received at an accredited American institution. Foreign education must be evaluated by an accredited private credential-evaluation organisation. The applicant must submit: The equivalency-evaluation letter A course-by-course assessment Supporting transcripts Any other required documentation Failure to provide the required foreign-education evaluation by the closing date may result in the application receiving no consideration. Conditions of Employment Selected applicants must satisfy several conditions, including: United States citizenship Continued qualifying student status Maintenance of a minimum 2.5 GPA Completion of a Pathways participant agreement Successful completion of a background investigation Ability to obtain and maintain the required security determination Compliance with applicable federal-employment requirements The announcement identifies the position as noncritical-sensitive or moderate risk and requires a Secret security clearance . Salary and Benefits The annual salary range is: $46,610–$60,593 The final amount will be determined according to the applicable GS-5 pay rules and the candidate’s official appointment. NDU’s stated employee benefits may include: Retirement coverage Social Security Thrift Savings Plan participation Health insurance Life insurance Long-term care insurance Paid vacation Sick leave Federal holidays Flexible schedules Transit subsidy Telework opportunities Eligibility for particular benefits may depend on the appointment type, length and other federal-employment rules. Required Application Documents Applicants must submit a complete application package. Two-Page Résumé The vacancy requires a federal résumé of no more than two pages. The résumé should demonstrate how the applicant meets the experience requirements and should include relevant examples of: Research Administrative support Document preparation Data collection Literature review Archival work Academic projects Volunteer experience Technology skills Applicants should not upload a long academic CV and assume the system will locate the useful fragments buried on page seven. The two-page limit is explicit. Academic Transcript Current transcripts are required from all applicants. The transcript must show: The applicant’s name The institution’s name Relevant courses Credit hours Academic standing Evidence of the required GPA An unofficial transcript may be accepted at the application stage. Proof of Enrolment or Acceptance Students who are not yet currently enrolled must provide an acceptance letter confirming at least part-time enrolment. Eligibility Documents Applicants claiming military-spouse, veteran or other federal hiring preferences must submit the relevant documents listed in the vacancy. Candidates are responsible for confirming that all uploaded files are complete, legible and successfully received. USA Hire Assessment The recruitment process uses the USA Hire Assessment. After submitting the initial USAJOBS application, candidates may receive an email containing a unique link to the assessment platform. Applicants should: Review the assessment instructions carefully. Reserve sufficient uninterrupted time. Use the unique link connected to their USAJOBS credentials. Complete all required assessments by the stated deadline. Request reasonable accommodation before beginning the assessment where needed. The announcement advises applicants to reserve up to three hours, although many candidates may finish sooner. How Applications Will Be Evaluated The agency will compare: The résumé Academic and eligibility documents Occupational-questionnaire responses USA Hire Assessment results Evidence of specialised experience Satisfaction of minimum requirements Eligible applicants will be placed into one of three categories: Qualified The applicant meets the minimum qualification requirements. Highly Qualified The applicant exceeds the minimum requirements and demonstrates proficiency in relevant competencies. Best Qualified The applicant exceeds the requirements and demonstrates a high level of proficiency in the assessed competencies. Veterans’ preference and other applicable federal priority rules may affect referral and selection order. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through USAJOBS. Applicants should: Open the official vacancy announcement. Select “Apply.” Create or sign in to a USAJOBS account. Complete the eligibility and occupational questionnaires. Upload the required résumé and supporting documents. Select and attach every document to the application. Submit the application. Complete any required USA Hire assessments. Return to USAJOBS to verify the application status. Applicants who reopen an incomplete application may need to reselect and reattach their résumé and supporting documents before resubmitting. APPLY HERE Application Deadline Applications close on: 27 August 2026 However, the agency will close the announcement once it receives 100 applications , even when that occurs before the listed closing date. Applying early is therefore essential. Waiting until 27 August may be a perfectly legal plan and a strategically terrible one. Conclusion The National Defense University Student Trainee Internship 2026 offers a paid entry point into federal public service for students interested in national security, defence policy, strategic research and international affairs. The selected trainee will support faculty and senior staff through document preparation, basic research, information gathering, archival work and literature review. The position also provides practical exposure to the research environment of a major United States national-security institution. Applicants must be United States citizens, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5, remain enrolled at least half-time for Fall 2026 and live or attend school within the Washington, DC commuting area. They must also provide a two-page résumé, academic transcripts and any applicable eligibility documents. The role pays $46,610–$60,593 per year and may provide eligibility for eventual non-competitive conversion to permanent federal employment, although conversion is not guaranteed. Applications should be submitted as soon as possible because the announcement will close on 27 August 2026 or after 100 applications have been received, whichever comes first . For further information and application requirements, CLICK HERE . To discover more opportunities, VISIT HERE . title: CDRI ASEAN Scholar Fellowship 2026: Five-Month Research Fellowship for Mid- to Senior-Level ASEAN Researchers
summary: The Cambodia Development Resource Institute is accepting applications for the ASEAN Scholar Fellowship 2026 , a five-month regional research opportunity for outstanding mid- to senior-level researchers from ASEAN Member States other than Cambodia. The fellowship is offered under CDRI’s ASEAN Scholar Exchange and Regional Institutional Linkages Initiative. It is designed to strengthen collaboration among Southeast Asian research institutions while expanding the use of advanced quantitative methods, econometric modelling, statistical programming and artificial intelligence-informed analytical approaches in policy research. The selected ASEAN Scholar Fellow will complete a three-month in-person residency at CDRI in Phnom Penh, followed by two months of remote collaboration. During the fellowship, the scholar will mentor junior researchers, collaborate on policy-relevant research, produce joint knowledge products and help establish sustainable institutional relationships between CDRI and the Fellow’s home institution. Applications must be submitted by 15 August 2026 . About the Cambodia Development Resource Institute The Cambodia Development Resource Institute is an independent development policy research institute based in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. CDRI conducts policy-relevant research on Cambodia’s development challenges while contributing to broader regional discussions across Southeast Asia. Its work aims to strengthen evidence-based policymaking by producing rigorous research, supporting informed public dialogue and building research capacity. Through the ASEAN Scholar Exchange and Regional Institutional Linkages Initiative, CDRI seeks to deepen cooperation with universities, think tanks and research institutes throughout ASEAN. The ASEAN Scholar Fellowship forms part of this regional effort by bringing an experienced researcher into CDRI for a structured period of collaboration, mentorship and institutional exchange. The fellowship is supported by the Australian Government through The Asia Foundation’s Ponlok Chomnes II: Data and Dialogue for Development in Cambodia programme. Purpose of the ASEAN Scholar Fellowship The ASEAN Scholar Fellowship aims to strengthen regional research collaboration and improve institutional capacity in advanced quantitative policy research. Its principal objectives are to: Strengthen the technical research capabilities of CDRI’s junior researchers Provide mentorship in quantitative research and econometric modelling Expand knowledge of AI-informed analytical methods Promote collaborative research on shared ASEAN development challenges Encourage the production of policy-relevant research outputs Build lasting relationships between CDRI and regional research institutions Develop an active network of scholars committed to evidence-based policymaking Promote knowledge exchange across Southeast Asia The fellowship is therefore not simply a short research visit. It combines individual research, institutional capacity building, professional mentorship and regional partnership development. Fellowship Duration and Structure The ASEAN Scholar Fellowship will run for five months and includes two components. Three-Month Residency in Phnom Penh The selected Fellow will spend approximately three months working in person at CDRI in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The residency is expected to run from: Late August to late October 2026 During this period, the Fellow will work directly with CDRI researchers, participate in institutional activities and deliver technical mentorship and training. Two Months of Remote Collaboration Following the residency, the Fellow will continue collaborating remotely during: November and December 2026 The remote period will allow the Fellow and CDRI researchers to continue developing research outputs, finalise agreed deliverables and identify opportunities for future institutional cooperation. Applicants must therefore be available for both the in-person and remote portions of the fellowship. Main Responsibilities of the ASEAN Scholar Fellow Mentoring Junior Researchers A central responsibility of the Fellow will be to strengthen the technical skills of CDRI’s junior researchers. Mentorship may cover: Research design Quantitative analysis Econometric modelling Data management Statistical programming Evidence synthesis AI-informed research methods Machine-learning applications Interpretation of quantitative results Presentation of evidence for policy audiences The Fellow should be able to explain advanced methods clearly and adapt their guidance to researchers with different levels of experience. Collaborative Policy Research The Fellow will work with CDRI researchers on one or more collaborative policy-research projects. Projects should align with CDRI’s research priorities and address development issues relevant to Cambodia, the Mekong sub-region or ASEAN more broadly. Collaboration may involve: Developing research questions Designing methodologies Constructing or cleaning datasets Conducting statistical analysis Interpreting findings Drafting policy recommendations Preparing research outputs for publication Presenting results to relevant audiences Applicants are expected to propose research ideas in their application rather than waiting until the fellowship begins to define a possible area of collaboration. Producing Joint Knowledge Products The selected scholar will co-author one or more agreed outputs with CDRI researchers. Possible products include: A working paper A policy brief A methodological note A technical guide A research report Another agreed knowledge product The application should identify the outputs that the applicant expects to help deliver during the fellowship. Delivering a Research Seminar The Fellow must deliver at least one research seminar for CDRI researchers. The seminar may present: The Fellow’s previous research Findings from the collaborative project A methodological issue A development-policy question Lessons from regional research practice The seminar should encourage discussion and contribute to wider institutional learning. Delivering a Technical Workshop The Fellow must also deliver at least one technical workshop. The workshop should provide practical training related to the Fellow’s methodological expertise, such as: Applied econometrics Economic modelling Forecasting Statistical programming Data visualisation Machine learning AI-assisted research Cost-benefit or policy analysis Reproducible research practices Advising on Research Methods The selected scholar will provide technical advice on strengthening CDRI’s research methodologies and analytical practices. This may involve reviewing current approaches, recommending tools and identifying opportunities to improve research quality, efficiency or reproducibility. Supporting Institutional Collaboration The Fellow is expected to help establish sustained cooperation between CDRI and the institution with which the scholar is currently affiliated. Potential areas of collaboration may include: Joint research projects Researcher exchanges Co-authored publications Joint seminars Technical training Data collaboration Future funding proposals Regional policy networks Applicants should demonstrate an interest in building a relationship that extends beyond the five-month fellowship. Preparing a Fellowship Reflection At the end of the fellowship, the scholar must prepare a short reflection summarising: Activities completed Contributions made Lessons learned Research outputs developed Challenges encountered Opportunities for future cooperation Priority Areas of Expertise Applications are invited from scholars whose expertise aligns with one or more of the following areas. Economic Modelling and Forecasting Relevant expertise may include macroeconomic modelling, sectoral forecasting, policy simulations and quantitative scenario analysis. Development Economics Researchers may focus on poverty, inequality, social protection, public services, human development or other development-policy questions. Industrial and Trade Policy Relevant work may examine industrial development, global value chains, regional trade, productivity, competitiveness or economic transformation. Labour Economics Possible themes include employment, wages, skills, migration, informality, labour-market transitions and workforce development. Public Finance and Macroeconomic Policy This area may include taxation, public expenditure, fiscal policy, debt, inflation, economic growth or government financing. Data Science for Public Policy Applicants may bring expertise in large datasets, computational methods, machine learning, artificial intelligence, data visualisation or predictive analysis. Climate and Environmental Economics Relevant topics may include climate policy, natural-resource management, green growth, environmental valuation, climate finance and economic resilience. Digital Economy and Innovation Researchers may work on digital transformation, technology policy, artificial intelligence, innovation systems, digital inclusion or platform economies. Applicants with strong methodological skills that can be applied across several policy areas are especially encouraged to apply. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must meet the following conditions. Citizenship Applicants must hold citizenship in an ASEAN Member State other than Cambodia. This restriction is intended to strengthen cross-border knowledge exchange and research collaboration between Cambodia and other ASEAN countries. Academic Qualifications Applicants should hold either: A PhD in economics, public policy, development studies, data science, statistics or a closely related field; or Established postdoctoral researcher status in a relevant discipline Exceptional applicants with a master’s degree may also be considered if they have at least five years of substantial, relevant research experience. Current Institutional Affiliation Applicants must currently be affiliated with a: University Think tank Research institute The institution should be located within an ASEAN Member State. Research Record Candidates should demonstrate an established record of applied and policy-relevant research. Evidence may include: Peer-reviewed publications Working papers Policy briefs Research reports Technical studies Government or institutional research Other relevant professional outputs Quantitative Research Expertise Applicants should have strong expertise in one or more of the following: Advanced quantitative methods Econometric modelling Statistical analysis Economic forecasting Stata R Python Machine learning AI-assisted research techniques Mentorship Experience Applicants should have experience supervising or mentoring: Early-career researchers Junior analysts Graduate students Research assistants Other developing research professionals The selection process will consider not only technical expertise but also the candidate’s ability to transfer knowledge effectively. GEDSI Commitment Applicants should demonstrate a commitment to integrating gender equality, disability and social inclusion principles into: Research design Data collection Analysis Stakeholder engagement Policy recommendations Regional Knowledge Experience conducting policy research in Cambodia or the broader Mekong sub-region is desirable. This experience is not presented as an absolute requirement, but it may strengthen an application. English Proficiency Applicants must have excellent written and spoken English. The selected Fellow must be able to: Produce high-quality research outputs Collaborate effectively with CDRI researchers Deliver seminars and workshops Communicate technical material clearly Selection Criteria Applications will be assessed according to: Relevance and depth of the applicant’s expertise Strength of the applicant’s policy-research record Experience mentoring early-career researchers Quality and relevance of proposed research ideas Potential contribution to CDRI’s research capacity Methodological strengths Expected fellowship outputs Potential to build long-term institutional partnerships Alignment with Cambodia and ASEAN development priorities The selection committee will seek a candidate who combines technical excellence with practical collaboration and mentorship skills. Fellowship Support CDRI will provide the selected ASEAN Scholar Fellow with: A fellowship stipend Office space during the Phnom Penh residency Access to CDRI research facilities Library access Computing resources Access to relevant data infrastructure Opportunities to collaborate with CDRI researchers Connections with regional research and policy partners The call does not state the amount of the stipend or whether additional costs such as travel, accommodation, insurance or visa expenses will be covered. Applicants should confirm these conditions directly with CDRI before accepting an offer. Required Application Documents Applications must be submitted in English and should contain four separate documents, preferably in PDF format. All documents should be attached to one email. 1. Research and Collaboration Statement Applicants must submit a research and collaboration statement of no more than two pages. It should explain: The applicant’s main research expertise Methodological strengths Proposed contributions to mentoring and capacity building at CDRI Specific collaborative research ideas relevant to Cambodia or ASEAN Expected fellowship outputs Applicants should avoid presenting only broad research interests. Strong statements will propose a focused and feasible collaboration that can produce meaningful outputs within five months. 2. Curriculum Vitae The CV should include: Academic qualifications Current institutional affiliation Employment history Publications Policy-research outputs Technical skills Mentorship experience Relevant regional experience Professional networks or partnerships 3. Motivation Letter Applicants must submit a motivation letter of no more than one page. The letter should explain: Why the applicant is interested in the fellowship What the applicant hopes to gain How the applicant’s expertise aligns with CDRI’s research agenda Why the applicant is suited to the mentoring and institutional-exchange components 4. Recommendation Letter One recommendation letter is required from the applicant’s current institution. The letter should ideally confirm the applicant’s research expertise, institutional role and suitability for the fellowship. How to Apply The four required documents should be attached to a single email and submitted to: kanika.sao@cdri.org.kh Applicants should ensure that all required materials are complete and clearly labelled. Incomplete or late applications will not be considered. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further discussion. Questions may be directed to: Ms Sao Kanika: kanika.sao@cdri.org.kh Dr Ang Raksmey: raksmey.ang@cdri.org.kh For the full call for applications and additional information, CLICK HERE . Application Deadline Applications must be submitted no later than: 15 August 2026 Applicants should submit early enough to allow time to resolve email-delivery or document-formatting problems. Commitment to Inclusion CDRI strongly encourages applications from: Women researchers Scholars from underrepresented groups Individuals from marginalised communities within ASEAN Member States Applicants will still be assessed according to the stated academic, professional and research criteria. Conclusion The CDRI ASEAN Scholar Fellowship 2026 offers an experienced ASEAN researcher the opportunity to contribute directly to policy research, institutional capacity building and regional knowledge exchange. Over five months, the selected scholar will mentor junior researchers, collaborate on research relevant to Cambodia and ASEAN, deliver seminars and technical workshops, and produce joint knowledge products. The fellowship is particularly suited to mid- and senior-level researchers with advanced quantitative expertise, strong publication records and experience supervising early-career scholars. Applicants must be citizens of ASEAN Member States other than Cambodia, be affiliated with a university or research institution in the region and demonstrate the ability to contribute to both research and long-term institutional collaboration. Applications, including all four required documents, must be submitted by 15 August 2026 . To discover more fellowship opportunities, VISIT HERE . title: Court of Justice of the European Union Paid Traineeships 2026 for Young Graduates (Up to €2,400/Month)
summary: The Court of Justice of the European Union offers paid traineeship programmes for young graduates. Approximately 200 places are available each year in both the Court’s services (five months) and in the Members’ Chambers (three to five months). 10 to 12 week traineeships are available in the Interpretation Directorate. The Court also has a specific traineeship programme for national judges. Introduction The Court’s traineeship programme will provide you with valuable skills, hands-on experience, and the chance to contribute to the activities of the EU’s judicial institution. As a trainee, you will join a dynamic, multilingual environment, connecting with like-minded peers who uphold the EU’s fundamental values of democracy, rule of law and human rights. Traineeships for Young Graduates Young graduates will gain insight into the Court’s functions and carry out tasks to assist in the Court’s work. There are a limited number of traineeships available, approximately 200 per year. They can take place either in the Members’ Chambers – with Judges or Advocates General – or in the Court’s administrative services. Types of Traineeships 1. Traineeships in the Members’ Chambers Law graduates, particularly those with training in EU law, can apply for chamber traineeships with Judges and Advocates General – in either the Court of Justice or the General Court. As part of their duties, trainees participate in the Chamber’s work by carrying out various tasks relating to cases assigned to the Judge or Advocate General and which have not yet reached the deliberation stage in the proceedings. Duration Three to five months Two sessions every year: 1 March to 31 July 1 October to the end of February 2. Traineeships in the Services Service traineeships in the Court’s administrative departments are open to graduates of any field of study – in some departments, a degree in a specific field, namely law, may be required. As part of their duties, trainees learn about the specific tasks performed in each department and can gain practical experience under the supervision of experienced officials. Services accepting trainees The services that accept trainees are the Directorate for Human Resources Directorate for the Budget and Financial Affairs Directorate for Buildings and Security Directorate for Multilingualism (legal translation and interpretation) Library Directorate Research and Documentation Directorate Projects and Terminological Coordination Unit Protocol and Visits Directorate Information Technology Directorate Communication Directorate Legal Adviser on Administrative Matters Registry of the Court of Justice of the European Union Registry of the General Court of the European Union Duration Five months Two sessions every year: 1 March to 31 July 1 October to the end of February 3. Traineeships in Interpretation Young graduates of conference interpreting can apply for traineeships in the Interpretation Department. As part of their duties, trainee interpreters will refine their interpreting skills, particularly of legal content, under the supervision of experienced interpreters. This includes preparing files, terminology research and practical exercises in a “silent booth”. In order to apply, you must have at least two passive languages or a second active language. You must also be able to read French. Duration 10 to 12 weeks Applicant selection takes place once a year covering the entire judicial year. Eligibility In order to apply, you must: be a national of an EU Member State (exceptions may apply in duly justified cases) have a university degree or diploma in any field of study – however, for the Members’ Chambers, a degree in law, political science, economics or a related field is required have a thorough knowledge of an official EU language and a good knowledge of another EU language. A good knowledge of French or English is required. have not already held a post or undertaken a traineeship – either paid or unpaid – lasting more than six weeks in an EU institution or body Grant Trainees receive a grant equivalent to 75% of the minimum social wage for a skilled worker in Luxembourg – amounting to a grant of approximately €2,400 per month. This grant is not subject to the tax regime applicable to EU officials and other agents. Under certain conditions, trainees will receive a one-time travel allowance, currently set at €150. This remuneration does not apply to any traineeships carried out in the Members’ Chambers outside of the two fixed periods under a professional training course for which trainees also receive a grant, an allowance or remuneration from another source. How to Apply You can submit your application via EU CV Online . For traineeships taking place during the period between 1 March and 31 July, apply between July and September the year before. For traineeships taking place during the period between 1 October and the end of February, apply between February and April of the same year. For interpretation traineeships taking place during the entire judicial year, apply between July and September the year before. The specific application deadlines are listed on EU CV Online. You may be asked to submit copies of diplomas and/or certificates upon request as part of the pre-selection procedure. The Court’s human resources department will contact successful applicants. Please note that admission to a traineeship does not grant the trainee the status of EU official or servant. It also does not give the trainee any right or entitlement to recruitment. Application periods 1 March to 31 July traineeships: Apply between July and September the year before. 1 October to the end of February traineeships: Apply between February and April of the same year. Interpretation traineeships: Apply between July and September the year before. The specific application deadlines are listed on EU CV Online. You may be asked to submit copies of diplomas and/or certificates upon request as part of the pre-selection procedure. The Court’s human resources department will contact successful applicants. Please note that admission to a traineeship does not grant the trainee the status of EU official or servant. It also does not give the trainee any right or entitlement to recruitment. Inclusivity Programme for Persons with Disabilities The Court supports equal opportunities and equal treatment of candidates. It actively encourages candidates from a wide variety of backgrounds to apply for a traineeship if they fulfil the eligibility criteria. The Court has a specific programme to ensure access to traineeships for persons with disabilities. This programme offers 2 traineeships per traineeship period. These traineeships last for three to five months and take place either in the Members’ Chambers or in the administrative services. Fields available Legal affairs Administration Communications IT Legal translation Legal research The application is done via EU CV Online . When applying candidates will be asked to supply documentation specifying the level of their disability. This is to ensure that our medical service can evaluate any accommodating measures that need to be taken. Grant Trainees in this programme receive a monthly grant and a one-time travel allowance, the amounts of which are higher than those provided under the other traineeship programmes. Traineeships for National Judges National judges can take part in an exchange programme organised by the European Judicial Training Network (EJTN). Trainee judges can work in the Members’ Chambers (Judges and Advocates General) in the Court of Justice or the General Court, or in the Research and Documentation Directorate (DRD). As part of their duties, trainee judges act as legal secretaries or DRD administrators, depending on where they are assigned. There are a limited number of traineeships available, with up to 15 judges accepted annually. The traineeships last for between 6 and 12 months. Eligibility for National Judges In order to apply, you must: have held judicial office – as a judge or prosecutor – in an EU Member State for at least one year be familiar with EU law have perfect knowledge of an official EU language and a satisfactory knowledge of French, in order to be able to support the Members in the handling of case files and the drafting of decisions Payment Trainee judges do not receive any payment or compensation from the Court. Instead, they receive a daily allowance funded by the EJTN. How to Apply (National Judges) Applications must be submitted to the EJTN. You can find more information about the traineeships on the EJTN website . Duty of Discretion All trainees are subject to a duty of discretion – both during and after their traineeship – regarding all internal Court matters and documents. Trainees must seek approval from the relevant Member or head of department before publishing anything related to the traineeship. Before beginning their traineeship, they must also sign a solemn undertaking pledging to uphold this duty. title: Women’s World Banking Fall 2026 Internships | Remote Opportunities in Research and Policy Advocacy
summary: Women’s World Banking is now accepting applications for its Fall 2026 internship opportunities. Graduate students interested in international development, women’s economic empowerment, public policy, research, and financial inclusion have an exciting chance to gain practical experience with one of the world’s leading organizations dedicated to advancing women’s financial inclusion. With more than four decades of experience working alongside financial institutions, policymakers, investors, and development partners, Women’s World Banking has become a global leader in creating economic opportunities for women. The Fall 2026 internship program provides aspiring professionals with the opportunity to contribute to meaningful projects while developing valuable skills and expanding their professional networks. The organization is currently recruiting graduate student interns for two key positions within the Women’s World Banking Institute. About Women’s World Banking Women’s World Banking is a global nonprofit organization focused on expanding women’s financial inclusion and economic participation. For over 40 years, the organization has worked with financial institutions worldwide to design innovative financial products and services that meet the needs of women, particularly those who have been underserved by traditional financial systems. Through research, policy advocacy, leadership development, and strategic partnerships, Women’s World Banking helps create financial ecosystems that empower women entrepreneurs, workers, and consumers. The organization’s mission is to ensure that women have access to the financial tools, services, and opportunities needed to achieve economic security and resilience. Available Internship Opportunities Women’s World Banking is currently offering the following internship positions for Fall 2026: Research Intern – Women’s World Banking Institute The Research Intern will support the Institute’s ongoing work on women’s financial inclusion through both qualitative and quantitative research activities. Responsibilities may include: * Conducting literature reviews and background research * Supporting data collection and analysis * Assisting with report preparation and research publications * Contributing to evidence-based projects on financial inclusion * Supporting research initiatives that examine barriers and opportunities for women’s economic participation This internship is ideal for graduate students with strong analytical skills and an interest in research, economics, development studies, public policy, finance, or related fields. Policy Advocacy Intern – Women’s World Banking Institute The Policy Advocacy Intern will support research and policy initiatives related to women’s financial inclusion at both national and global levels. Key responsibilities may include: * Monitoring policy developments affecting women’s financial inclusion * Conducting policy research and analysis * Supporting advocacy initiatives and policy campaigns * Assisting with stakeholder engagement activities * Preparing policy briefs and supporting materials This role is particularly suitable for students interested in public policy, international development, governance, advocacy, economics, and gender equality. Internship Benefits Interns selected for the Women’s World Banking Fall 2026 program will benefit from: * Hands-on experience in international development * Exposure to global financial inclusion initiatives * Opportunities to work on real-world projects * Professional mentorship and guidance * Practical experience in research and policy development * Collaboration with experienced professionals and global partners * Flexible and remote working opportunities * Networking opportunities within the development and financial inclusion sectors Why Apply? The Women’s World Banking internship program offers more than just professional experience. It provides an opportunity to contribute to global efforts aimed at improving women’s economic empowerment and financial security. Interns will gain valuable insight into: * Gender-focused financial inclusion strategies * International development practices * Public policy and advocacy processes * Research methodologies * Stakeholder engagement and partnership development * Global economic empowerment initiatives For students considering careers in international development, public policy, economics, finance, social impact, or nonprofit leadership, this internship can serve as a strong foundation for future professional growth. Eligibility Criteria Applicants should demonstrate: * Current enrollment in a graduate degree program * Strong interest in international development and women’s economic empowerment * Excellent research and analytical skills * Strong written and verbal communication abilities * Ability to work independently and collaboratively * Interest in financial inclusion and gender-focused development initiatives Specific qualifications may vary depending on the internship position. About the Women’s World Banking Institute The Women’s World Banking Institute serves as the organization’s research and learning arm. The Institute generates evidence-based insights and policy recommendations designed to improve women’s access to financial services and strengthen economic opportunities worldwide. Through rigorous research and policy engagement, the Institute helps shape discussions around women’s financial inclusion and contributes to solutions that drive sustainable economic growth. Application Process Interested candidates should review the internship descriptions carefully and submit their applications through the official Women’s World Banking careers portal. Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since positions remain open until filled. Application Link Apply HERE Conclusion The Women’s World Banking Fall 2026 Internships provide graduate students with a unique opportunity to gain practical experience while contributing to one of the most important global development challenges—advancing women’s financial inclusion. Whether your interests lie in research, policy advocacy, economic development, or social impact, these internships offer meaningful work, professional growth, and the chance to support initiatives that improve the lives of women around the world. title: American Academy in Berlin Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027–2028 in Germany | Fully Funded Fellowship for Scholars, Journalists, Writers and Public Policy Professionals
summary: Applications are now open for the prestigious American Academy in Berlin Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027–2028 , a fully funded international fellowship that brings outstanding scholars, writers, journalists, legal experts, and public policy professionals to Berlin for a semester-long residency. The American Academy in Berlin is one of the leading transatlantic institutions dedicated to strengthening intellectual and cultural ties between the United States and Germany. Each year, the Academy selects approximately 25 exceptional individuals through a highly competitive process and awards fellowships that allow recipients to pursue independent projects while engaging with Germany’s vibrant intellectual and cultural community. Fellows reside at the historic Hans Arnhold Center, located on the shores of Lake Wannsee in Berlin, where they become part of an interdisciplinary community of scholars and practitioners. In addition to receiving generous financial support, fellows participate in lectures, discussions, readings, and other public programs that contribute to transatlantic dialogue. The deadline for applications is September 25, 2026. About the American Academy in Berlin The American Academy in Berlin is an independent, nonprofit institute for advanced study that supports distinguished individuals working in: Arts Humanities Social Sciences Law Journalism Public Policy The institution s primary mission is to strengthen intellectual, academic, and cultural connections between the United States and Germany. Through its flagship Berlin Prize Fellowship, the Academy provides a unique opportunity for experts and thought leaders to advance their work in a stimulating international environment while building meaningful professional connections across disciplines. Fellowship Benefits Successful applicants will receive a comprehensive fellowship package that includes: Monthly Stipend Fellows receive a generous monthly stipend of **$5,000** throughout their residency. Roundtrip Airfare The Academy covers roundtrip travel expenses between the fellow s home location and Berlin. Accommodation Recipients are provided accommodation at or near the Academy s historic **Hans Arnhold Center** on Lake Wannsee. Partial Board The fellowship includes partial meal support during the residency period. Library and Research Resources Fellows receive access to the Academy s in-house library services and research support. Professional Networking Opportunities Participants become part of an influential network of academics, policymakers, journalists, writers, and public intellectuals. Public Engagement Opportunities Fellows present their work through: Public lectures Readings Panel discussions Film screenings Performances Academic events Fields and Disciplines Eligible for the Fellowship The Academy welcomes applications from individuals working in: Humanities Including history, philosophy, literature, religious studies, and related fields. Social Sciences Including sociology, political science, anthropology, economics, and related disciplines. Law Projects examining legal systems, public policy, governance, and justice. Journalism Investigative journalists, reporters, editors, and media professionals. Public Policy Professionals and researchers working on policy development and implementation. Specialized Fellowship Areas The Academy also offers dedicated support for projects in: Jewish Studies German Studies Public Health Biotechnology Priority Themes Although projects do not need to focus specifically on Germany, applicants are encouraged to explain how a residency in Berlin would enhance their work. The Academy particularly welcomes projects addressing pressing global issues such as: Democracy Security Technology and Society Artificial Intelligence (AI) Climate and Energy International Relations Global Order Public Health Who Can Apply? The fellowship is intended for individuals who demonstrate excellence in their respective fields. Eligible applicants include: Scholars Researchers Writers Journalists Legal Experts Public Policy Professionals Public Intellectuals Applicants should possess a strong record of professional achievement and a compelling project proposal. Who Cannot Apply? According to the Academy s guidelines: Visual artists must apply through separate nomination-based competitions. Composers are selected through separate nomination processes. Project proposals in mathematics and the natural sciences are generally not accepted. Residency Experience in Berlin Fellows live and work in Berlin while becoming part of an active intellectual community. The residency offers: Time and space for focused research and writing. Interaction with scholars and experts from different disciplines. Opportunities to engage with German institutions and organizations. Access to cultural and academic events. Participation in media and public engagement activities. The fellowship experience is designed to encourage meaningful exchange between American and German intellectual communities. Application Process Interested applicants should complete the online application before the deadline. Applicants should prepare all required application materials, including project information and supporting documentation as outlined in the official application portal. Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues. Why You Should Apply The Berlin Prize Fellowship is one of the most respected international fellowship programs available to scholars, journalists, writers, and policy professionals. The combination of financial support, accommodation, research time, public engagement opportunities, and access to Berlin s dynamic intellectual environment makes this an exceptional opportunity for professionals seeking to advance impactful projects. For those interested in contributing to international dialogue while benefiting from a world-class academic and cultural environment, the American Academy in Berlin Fellowship offers a transformative experience. Conclusion The American Academy in Berlin Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027–2028 provides an outstanding opportunity for scholars, journalists, writers, legal experts, and public policy professionals to spend a semester in Germany pursuing meaningful projects while engaging with an influential international community. With a monthly stipend of $5,000, accommodation, airfare, networking opportunities, and access to exceptional intellectual resources, the fellowship offers the ideal environment for advancing innovative ideas and impactful work. Interested applicants should submit their applications before September 25, 2026. Discover more fellowship opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage . title: UNICEF Youth Advisors 2026: Join the Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM)
summary: Applications are now open for the UNICEF Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM) Youth Advisors 2026. UNICEF is seeking five young people aged 18–24 with lived experience of mental health and a passion for improving child and adolescent mental health (CAMH) data to join its global Technical Advisory Group for a two-year term . Youth advisors will work alongside leading researchers, practitioners, and technical experts to shape how UNICEF measures, tracks, and uses data on children s and adolescents mental health worldwide. Successful applicants will receive a USD 2,000 stipend over two years , travel support for in-person meetings, and opportunities to co-author technical outputs and participate in global advocacy initiatives. About the UNICEF TAG-CAMHM Youth Advisor Programme Mental health conditions are among the leading causes of illness and disability among adolescents globally. However, reliable and youth-informed data on child and adolescent mental health remains limited. To strengthen global mental health measurement, UNICEF is establishing the Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM) —an independent body comprising researchers, practitioners, and youth advisors. As a Youth Advisor, you will serve as a full and equal member of the Technical Advisory Group, bringing your lived experiences and perspectives to influence how mental health data is collected, interpreted, and used. Key Summary Opportunity Details Organisation UNICEF Programme Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM) – Youth Advisors Position Youth Advisor (5 positions available) Who Can Apply? Young people aged 18–24 with lived experience of mental health and engagement in child and adolescent mental health (CAMH)-related work Location Global (applications encouraged from all regions, especially the Global South) Duration Two-year advisory term (renewable) Stipend USD 1,000 per year (USD 2,000 over the two-year term) Benefits Equal membership on the Technical Advisory Group, fully funded travel for in-person meetings, mentorship, networking, opportunities to co-author publications, and participation in UNICEF initiatives Meetings Two per year (one virtual and one in-person/hybrid) Application Deadline 17 August 2026 How to Apply Submit a one-page statement of interest and a CV/resume (or approved alternative format) via email Application Email ITY-CAMH-Data@unicef.org Email Subject Youth Advisor Expression of Interest – TAG Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement Why This Matters Mental health conditions are among the leading causes of illness and disability among adolescents around the world. Yet the data and evidence that should be driving responses, including who is affected, how, and where, remain incomplete, inconsistently collected, and too rarely shaped by the perspectives of young people themselves. UNICEF is working to change that. UNICEF will convene a Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM), an independent group of researchers, practitioners, and youth advisors who will help shape how UNICEF measures, tracks, and uses data on children s and adolescents mental health. We are seeking five young people aged 18 to 24 to join the TAG as youth advisors. Youth advisors are full and equal members of the group. You would be contributing your lived experience and perspectives alongside senior researchers and technical experts, with equal standing in all discussions. What the Role Involves A. Advising on CAMH measurement As a full TAG member, you will: Attend and actively participate in TAG meetings twice a year. One meeting will be in person or hybrid and one will be virtual. Review documents and provide input on UNICEF s measurement tools and initiatives, including MMAPP, from the perspective of a young person with lived experience Share your views on what data young people need, how it should be collected, and how it should be used Contribute thought leadership on youth-focused and youth-led CAMH measurement: what data young people need, how it should be collected, and how it should be used Participate in working groups or ad hoc consultations as relevant B. Data and Research for Decision-Making workstream Youth advisors will also contribute to a related piece of UNICEF work focused on helping young people and governments use data and research more effectively in mental health decision-making. This workstream is developing two practical learning experiences: one designed for young people, and one designed for governments and implementing organisations. Both are built around real mental health data scenarios, and a third session brings both groups together to engage with each other around shared evidence. Your contribution to this work will involve: Co-designing the learning experience for young people, including the scenario content, facilitation approach, and associated guidance materials Contributing your perspective to the framework that guides how both tools are designed and used Providing input into related guidance and toolkit materials as they are developed C. Youth-identified activities Beyond these two areas, advisors are encouraged to propose additional contributions based on their own expertise and interests, such as co-authorship of technical papers, participation in advocacy forums, or engagement in related UNICEF initiatives. These are agreed with the Secretariat on an ongoing basis and form part of the overall engagement. Who We Are Looking For We are looking for five young people aged 18 to 24 at the time of recruitment, with lived experience of mental health and demonstrated engagement in CAMH-related work. You do not need to be a researcher or hold a formal academic qualification. What matters is your experience, your perspective, and your commitment to making sure that data and evidence on children s and adolescents mental health reflects and serves the communities most affected. You may be a strong candidate if you have experience in one or more of the following areas: Advocating for better mental health policy, services, or systems at a national or international level Participating in or leading community-based or youth-led research or data collection on mental health Leading or playing an active role in a youth-led organisation focused on mental health, wellbeing, or children s rights Working to influence mental health policies, systems, or funding Using data or research to support mental health advocacy or to inform how programmes are designed UNICEF strongly encourages applications from young people based in or with substantial experience in the Global South, including Sub-Saharan Africa, South and South-East Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, the Middle East and North Africa, and Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Diversity of background, thought, identity, and experience is essential to the work of the TAG. What UNICEF Offers Stipend USD 1,000 per year (USD 2,000 total over the two-year term), recognising the full scope of your engagement across TAG advisory activities, workstream co-design, and youth-identified contributions. Equal standing Youth advisors are full TAG members with equal voice in all deliberations — not observers or a separate youth panel. Your input carries the same weight as that of senior researchers and technical experts. Travel and support Travel and accommodation for in-person TAG meetings are covered by UNICEF for all youth members. You will receive tailored pre-meeting orientation, briefing materials in accessible language, and preparatory calls with the Secretariat as needed. Peer connections The Secretariat will facilitate connections between youth advisors and senior technical experts on the TAG, to support learning, mentorship, and collaboration. Recognition and opportunities TAG membership is a recognised advisory role that may be referenced on your CV and professional profiles. Advisors will have opportunities to co-author technical outputs, attend and speak at relevant events, and engage in related UNICEF initiatives as part of the role. Conditions of Appointment Youth advisors serve a two-year term, with the possibility of renewal All advisors serve in their individual capacity and do not represent any government, organisation, or institution Members are required to complete a Declaration of Interests before appointment and to maintain confidentiality regarding TAG discussions The working language of the TAG is English Stipend payments are linked to active participation. Advisors are expected to engage meaningfully across the full scope of the role. How to Apply To express interest in serving as a TAG youth advisor, please submit the following to ITY-CAMH-Data@unicef.org by August 17 , using the subject line Youth Advisor Expression of Interest – TAG Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement : A short statement (maximum one page) describing your interest in the role, what you would bring to the TAG, and any relevant experience in CAMH advocacy, research, or evidence use. Write in whatever way feels natural to you. Please include a note of any conflicts of interest relevant to your participation. A brief CV/resume or professional profile (maximum two pages), including relevant experience, initiatives you have been involved in, or organisations you are part of We recognise that not everyone has a traditional CV/resume. If you would prefer to share your experience in a different format, for example a portfolio, a short video, or a written description of your work, please contact us before the deadline to discuss alternatives. Due to the expected volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. UNICEF may hold conversations with shortlisted candidates as part of the selection process. Selection is at UNICEF s sole discretion, taking into account lived experience, engagement in CAMH-related work, geographic and identity diversity, and communication skills. For questions, please write to ITY-CAMH-Data@unicef.org well before the deadline. SOURCE: UNICEF CLICK HERE FOR FULL DETAILS The post UNICEF Youth Advisors 2026: Join the Technical Advisory Group on Child and Adolescent Mental Health Measurement (TAG-CAMHM) appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: DAFI Scholarship Programme 2026/2027 in Rwanda: Fully Funded Undergraduate Scholarships for Refugees and Asylum Seekers
summary: Applications Deadline: 7 August 2026 Are you a refugee or asylum seeker in Rwanda looking to pursue a university education? Applications are now open for the UNHCR Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative (DAFI) Scholarship Programme for the 2026/2027 academic year . The DAFI Scholarship is a fully funded higher education programme that enables qualified refugee and returnee students to earn an undergraduate degree or accredited technical qualification in their country of asylum or home country. Since its inception, the programme has transformed the lives of thousands of refugee students worldwide, including more than 600 scholars in Rwanda . If you meet the eligibility requirements, this is your opportunity to access quality higher education while developing leadership, professional, and community engagement skills. About the UNHCR DAFI Scholarship Programme The DAFI (Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative) Scholarship Programme is managed by UNHCR and supports refugee students in pursuing undergraduate (Bachelor s) degrees and selected Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes. The scholarship supports programmes classified under: ISCED Level 6: Bachelor s degrees or equivalent qualifications ISCED Level 5: Accredited TVET programmes lasting two years or more, leading to a diploma or certification Beyond financial assistance, DAFI scholars receive continuous academic support, mentorship, and opportunities to participate in leadership, skills development, and community engagement activities throughout their studies. Please note: The DAFI Scholarship does not fund Master s degree programmes. DAFI Scholarship Benefits The scholarship package varies depending on the country but generally covers: Full tuition fees Study materials and learning resources Food allowance Transportation costs Accommodation support Academic monitoring and student support Leadership and community engagement opportunities DAFI Scholarship Eligibility Criteria (Rwanda) To be eligible, applicants must: Be a recognized refugee or asylum seeker living in Rwanda Demonstrate strong academic performance (priority is given to outstanding students) Have been admitted to a university in Rwanda and provide proof of admission Not currently be receiving another higher education scholarship Not have been approved for resettlement to a third country Ensure that only one member per family applies or receives the DAFI Scholarship Additional Selection Considerations UNHCR particularly encourages applications from: Female applicants Persons with disabilities or special educational needs Required Documents Applicants must upload the following documents: UNHCR Proof of Registration Official or certified copy of high school diploma University admission letter or proof of acceptance from a university in Rwanda Equivalence certificate issued by the Ministry of Education of the country of asylum Ensure that all documents are complete before submitting your application. How to Apply for the DAFI Scholarship 2026/2027 Eligible applicants must complete the online DAFI application form and upload all required supporting documents before the application deadline. All application should be submitted through DAFI online application form, available at the following link: Rwanda 2026 DAFI Call for applications Application Deadline Opening Date: 15 July 2026 Closing Date: 7 August 2026 Late or incomplete applications will not be considered. Need Application Support? Applicants experiencing internet connectivity challenges or difficulties uploading documents can seek assistance from: The nearest Digital Career Counsellor in their refugee camp A nearby Community Centre For any inquiries, please contact us via rwakibarizahano@unhcr.org and aurea_kagwesage@wvi.org Final Thoughts The UNHCR DAFI Scholarship Programme 2026/2027 provides refugee and asylum-seeking students in Rwanda with an invaluable opportunity to obtain a fully funded undergraduate education while building the knowledge, leadership, and professional skills needed for future success. If you meet the eligibility criteria, be sure to submit your application before 7 August 2026 . All application should be submitted through DAFI online application form, available at the following link: Rwanda 2026 DAFI Call for applications For more scholarships and educational opportunities, keep visiting Opportunities For Youth.
