title: Heinrich Böll Foundation Tailwind for Talents Scholarships 2026/2027 in Germany for International Master’s and PhD Students
summary: Germany continues to be one of the world s most attractive destinations for higher education, offering internationally recognized universities, world-class research institutions, and numerous funding opportunities for outstanding students from around the globe. One of the most prestigious opportunities currently open is the Heinrich Böll Foundation Tailwind for Talents Scholarship Program, designed specifically to support talented international graduate students and doctoral candidates from developing countries who wish to study in Germany. The Heinrich Böll Foundation is committed to promoting equal opportunities, educational access, academic excellence, sustainability, democracy, human rights, and social responsibility. Through this scholarship program, the foundation seeks to empower future leaders who demonstrate exceptional academic potential, social engagement, and a commitment to creating positive change within their communities and beyond. Whether you are planning to pursue a Master s degree or embark on a PhD journey in Germany, this scholarship can significantly reduce your financial burden while providing access to a vibrant international academic community and numerous professional development opportunities. About the Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship The Tailwind for Talents Scholarship is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA). It is specifically designed to provide financial and academic support to international students from eligible developing countries who aspire to continue their education in Germany. Beyond financial assistance, scholarship recipients become part of a dynamic network of scholars, researchers, professionals, and alumni who are actively engaged in shaping a more democratic, environmentally sustainable, and socially just world. The scholarship combines financial funding with extensive academic support, networking opportunities, leadership development, and participation in educational events organized by the Heinrich Böll Foundation. Why Choose the Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship? The scholarship is more than financial support—it is an investment in future global leaders. Successful applicants benefit from: Financial support throughout their studies. Funding supported by the German government. Opportunities to study at leading German universities. Access to academic mentoring and professional guidance. Participation in seminars, workshops, conferences, and networking events. Leadership development opportunities. Membership in an international community of scholars. Access to an extensive alumni network. Opportunities for interdisciplinary learning. Exposure to Germany s academic, research, and innovation ecosystem. Support services that help students successfully settle into academic life in Germany. Who Can Apply? The scholarship welcomes applications from outstanding international students who meet the eligibility requirements. For Master s Students Applicants must: Have completed their first university degree outside Germany. Intend to begin a Master s degree at a university in Germany. Submit their application before commencing their Master s studies in Germany. Demonstrate academic excellence and motivation. The foundation gives priority consideration to applicants from OECD DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany at the time they apply. For PhD Applicants Applicants must: Have completed a graduate degree outside Germany. Intend to pursue a PhD at a recognized German institution. Meet the academic requirements for doctoral study in Germany. Demonstrate strong research potential and commitment to societal impact. Priority is also given to applicants from OECD DAC countries who have not yet established residence in Germany. Scholarship Benefits Although individual funding may vary depending on the applicant s academic level and circumstances, recipients receive comprehensive support that may include: Financial assistance to support living expenses. Academic support throughout the duration of study. Participation in educational seminars. Professional development activities. Leadership and civic engagement training. Networking with scholars from around the world. Access to the Heinrich Böll Foundation s extensive alumni community. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration. Ongoing mentoring and institutional support. Academic Support Beyond Funding One distinguishing feature of the Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship is its holistic approach to supporting scholars. Recipients benefit from various non-financial opportunities, including: Academic Development Research support. Academic mentoring. Workshops and seminars. Educational events. Professional Development Leadership training. Communication skills development. Networking opportunities. Career guidance. Community Engagement The foundation encourages scholars to actively contribute to society by participating in: Social initiatives. Environmental sustainability projects. Democratic engagement. Human rights advocacy. Civic participation. Application Process Applicants should carefully review all official application documents before submitting their applications. Separate application guides are available for: Master s degree applicants. PhD applicants. These guides contain detailed eligibility requirements, required documents, application procedures, and submission instructions. Prospective applicants are also encouraged to review the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ), which provides clarification on the selection process and online application procedures. Important Application Deadlines Applicants should note the following application periods: Fall 2026 Intake Application Opens: 15 July 2026 Application Deadline: 1 September 2026 Spring 2027 Intake Application Opens: 15 January 2027 Application Deadline: 1 March 2027 Applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare their documents well in advance to avoid last-minute submission challenges. Required Preparation Before Applying Before beginning your application, it is advisable to: Confirm your eligibility. Review the official application information sheet. Gather all required supporting documents. Prepare any required academic statements. Ensure your academic qualifications meet German university admission requirements. Read the Frequently Asked Questions. Submit your application before the relevant deadline. Why Study in Germany? Germany has become one of the world s leading destinations for international higher education due to: High-quality universities. Strong research infrastructure. Internationally recognized degrees. Excellent career opportunities. Diverse academic community. Affordable education compared to many other study destinations. Strong links between academia and industry. Rich cultural experiences. Receiving a Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship further enhances this experience by providing financial stability and access to an influential network of scholars and professionals. Contact Information Applicants seeking additional information may contact: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship Department Schumannstraße 8 10117 Berlin, Germany Telephone: +49 (0) 30 285 34-400 Fax: +49 (0) 30 285 34-409 Email: studienwerk@boell.de Office Hours: Monday Tuesday Thursday Friday 10:00 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. (Germany Time) For more information about this scholarship, visit the Heinrich Böll Foundation Tailwind for Talents Scholarship HERE For more scholarships opportunities visit OFY Website HERE Conclusion The Heinrich Böll Foundation Tailwind for Talents Scholarship represents an outstanding opportunity for ambitious international students from eligible developing countries who aspire to pursue advanced studies in Germany. title: OHCHR Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027: Fully Funded UN Human Rights Fellowship in Geneva
summary: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) is now accepting applications for the Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027 . This prestigious, fully funded fellowship offers indigenous leaders from around the world an opportunity to strengthen their knowledge of the United Nations human rights system and gain practical skills to advance and protect the rights of indigenous peoples. The programme brings together fellows from different regions and language backgrounds for an intensive four-week training in Geneva, Switzerland , while providing a unique opportunity to engage directly with UN human rights mechanisms. Key Summary Host: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) Programme: Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027 Location: Geneva, Switzerland Duration: 4 weeks (June/July 2027) Funding: Fully funded (return airfare, living expenses, and basic health insurance) Languages: English, French, Spanish, and Portuguese Eligibility: Indigenous persons nominated by an indigenous organization or community Education Requirement: No formal educational qualifications required Application Deadline: 6 September 2026 (23:59 Geneva time) Application Method: Online application with a recommendation letter from the nominating indigenous organization or community General information: The Indigenous Fellowship Programme was launched in 1997 by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in the context of the first International Decade of the World s Indigenous People. The aim of the programme is to give indigenous persons the opportunity to gain knowledge about the UN system and mechanisms dealing with human rights issues in general and indigenous issues in particular. Trained participants are better equipped to assist their organisations and communities in protecting and promoting their rights. This training programme is available in 4 languages: English , Spanish , French and Portuguese . When does it take place? Fellows from all 4 language components of the programme are trained together with simultaneous interpretation over 4 weeks in Geneva . The date of the training programme usually coincides with the annual session of the Expert Mechanism on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples ( June/July each year), allowing the fellows to participate more actively in that Mechanism. What does the programme cover? The selected candidates are entitled to a return flight ticket, living expenses and basic health insurance for the duration of the training. Who can apply for the programme? The candidate must be indigenous (non-indigenous persons will not be taken into consideration, even if they have close links with indigenous communities and/or organizations). Indigenous candidates, including women, LGBTQI+ individuals, and persons with disabilities, are strongly encouraged to apply. Age should not be a limitation to participation in the programme. Formal education should not be a limitation to participation in the IFP given the socio-economic barriers confronted by many indigenous peoples that limit access to formal educational institutions. Candidates should agree to train other indigenous persons after the return to their respective communities/organizations. The candidate should be proposed, and his/her candidacy supported by his/her indigenous organization and/or community. It is desirable that the sponsoring organization has a firm constituency or membership and that it is representative. The candidate should have a good working knowledge of the language in which the programme is imparted. Application procedure: We strongly encourage you to submit you online application well before the deadline of 6 September 2026 (23:59 Geneva time) . Fellowship applications will only be taken into consideration if they are fully completed. Both parts I and II of the application form must be completed Application forms must include an official recommendation letter from the nominating Indigenous organization or community. Applicants should upload their recommendation letters directly to the online application form. The application form is available at: https://survey.ohchr.org/429282?lang=en Selection process: The selection of fellows reflects a gender and regional balance, as well as a balance between communities represented. The general human rights situation in the respective regions/countries is also taken into consideration. A pre-selection of 15 to 20 candidates per language group is made by previous indigenous fellows. The selection process also entails interviews of pre-selected candidates who applied to either the English, French, Spanish or Portuguese language components of the programme. The final selection of successful candidates is reviewed by an advisory group composed of OHCHR staff. In view of the large number of applications, ONLY PRE-SELECTED CANDIDATES ARE CONTACTED. Any other questions? Any question pertaining to the Indigenous Fellowship Programme can be e-mailed to: ohchr-fellowship@un.org .
